exposure: network gatekeeping mechanisms (localization, infrastructure, cost effect, channeling, censorship, regulation, editorial, user-interaction and value adding mechanisms)
outcome: information benefits for vulnerable pregnant women
cohort: Members and administrators of a Facebook Vaginal Birth After Cesarean (VBAC) Group with over 500 pregnant women in rural Appalachia in the United States.
finding: Implementations of nine network gatekeeping mechanisms by VBAC group administrators help control interactions and information on the group, thereby creating 16 information benefits for vulnerable pregnant women before, during and after pregnancy.
mod_finding: The study explores how gatekeepers in a VBAC Facebook group aim to transform a doctor-centric birth culture to a more mother-centric one, directly relating to choices and perceptions around mode of birth.
